extensionDescription.message: Sort and deduplicate tabs while respecting tab groups. Includes custom ordering, auto-sort, and English / Chinese settings.

actionTitle.message: Sort tabs · Super Tab Sorter Next

tagline.message: A little order for your open tabs.

sortHelp.message: URL sorts by domain, then subdomain and path. Custom follows the existing order of website hosts.

dedupeTabs.message: Close duplicate tabs, keeping the newest

dedupeHelp.message: Deduplicate by the selected rule within each group or the ungrouped area. Pinned tabs are handled separately when included in sorting.

preserveOrderWithinGroups.message: Keep tab order within the same website

intervalHelp.message: 1–3600 seconds; default 300. Intervals of 60 seconds or more round up to whole minutes. Browser sleep or background suspension can delay sorting, especially below 60 seconds.

autoSortOnTabCreate.message: Also sort when a tab opens

autoSortOnTabClose.message: Also sort when a tab closes

suspendedHelp.message: For The Great Suspender derivatives using suspended.html#uri=… URLs, such as The Marvellous Suspender. Otherwise, keep the defaults.

groupSuspendedTabs.message: Move suspended tabs together to the left

error.message: Something went wrong. Reopen this page and try again.

usage.message: Click the toolbar icon to sort the last focused window. Right-click the icon and choose Options to return here. Auto-sort uses that same window; it does not sort every window.

groupsHelp.message: Native tab groups are preserved and sorted by name. Prefix names with numbers (01 Work, 02 Reading) to control their order. Automatic sorting is off by default.

privacyText.message: Tab URLs, titles and group information are processed inside your browser only to sort and deduplicate tabs. No browsing history is stored or sent to the developer. Preferences, including your language choice, use Chrome storage sync and may sync through your Google account. No analytics, ads or remote code.

limitedUse.message: Use of information received from Google APIs adheres to the Chrome Web Store User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements.

regexHelp.message: The first matching rule replaces the URL for comparison only. Unmatched URLs and empty results use the original URL. Enter a JavaScript regex without / delimiters; replacements support capture groups such as $1 and $2.

ruleFlags.message: Flags (optional: g i m s u)

testUrls.message: Test URLs (one per line; uses unsaved rules and never closes tabs)

invalidRule.message: Enter a valid regular expression and flags (g i m s u only, without duplicates).

noRuleMatch.message: No matching rule; using the full URL
